summary: Alaka Chudal is an Indologist and linguist who completed a PhD at the University of Vienna (2009–2014). She served as a Lecturer at Nepal Sanskrit University (1995–2007) and held a post at the University of Vienna in 2007.

Alan Avdagić works in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Jena (BA, 2019–2023) and the University of Würzburg (MA, 2023–2025), holding posts at Würzburg and the Free University of Berlin (attested 2026).
Alan Butterworth (1864–1937) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He was educated at Elizabeth College (circa 1877–1883) and Balliol College, Oxford (1883).

Alan Coates Bouquet (1884–1976) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Educated at University College London, Trinity College, Cambridge (BA, ~1902–1905), and Jesus College, Cambridge, he served as Lecturer in History and Comparative Study of Religion at Cambridge (1924–1955).

Alan Entwistle (1949–1996) studied Indology and religious studies at Southampton and SOAS, earning a PhD under J. C. Wright. He held posts at the University of Groningen (1980–1985) and the University of Washington (Assistant Professor 1986, Associate Professor 1990).

Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Johns Hopkins (BA, 1973–1977) and Temple University (PhD, 1980–1988), later serving as Professor (1990, 1992) and Associate Professor of Philosophy (attested 2013–2014) at the University of Delaware.

Alan Gerard Wagner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2008) under Parimal G. Patil, having also studied under Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.
Alan Gowans (1923–2001) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He was educated at the University of Toronto (1946) and Princeton University (1948, 1950).

Alan John Bayard Wace (1879–1957) was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Pembroke College, Cambridge under Robert Alexander Neil. He held positions at the British School at Athens, Victoria and Albert Museum, Cambridge, and Alexandria University.
Alan Lomax (1915–2002) was an American scholar who pursued studies at Harvard University (~1932–1933), the University of Texas at Austin (~1933–1936), and Columbia University (~1939–1940).
Alan Nussbaum (born 1947) is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Harvard University (~1969–1976) and became a Professor at Cornell University in 1985.

Alan Sponberg (1944–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from the University of British Columbia. He held faculty posts at Princeton University (attested 1980–1987) and Stanford University (attested 1988).

Alan Watts (1915–1973) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Bexley Seabury Seminary, he served as Northwestern University's Episcopal chaplain (1944–1950), taught at the American Academy of Asian Studies (1951–1957), and joined the Esalen Institute.

Alasdair MacIntyre (1929–2025) was a philosopher educated at Queen Mary University of London and the University of Manchester. His academic career included positions at Essex, Brandeis, Notre Dame (~1989–2010), Duke, and London Metropolitan University.

Alasdair Urquhart (born 1945) is a philosopher educated at the University of Edinburgh (MA, ~1963–1967) and the University of Pittsburgh (PhD, ~1967–1973). He taught at the University of Toronto Mississauga before becoming Emeritus Professor at Toronto in 1986.

Alastair Gornall is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who completed a PhD at the University of Cambridge (2009–2013). He has held positions at the Singapore University of Technology and Design, SOAS, and the Pali Text Society.

Albert Benjamin Norton (1847–1923) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his studies at Northwestern University (~1867–1871) and Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary (~1871–1872).

Albert Cuny (1869–1947) was a linguist who earned his PhD at the Sorbonne (1907) under Victor Henry, Sylvain Lévi, and Antoine Meillet. He taught at Lycée Edmond Perrier and became a Professor at the University of Bordeaux (1910–1937).

Albert Debrunner (1884–1958) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Basel (1907) under Jacob Wackernagel. He held professorships at Zurich, Greifswald, Jena, and notably Bern (1920; 1935–1954), as well as teaching at Basel (1940–1949).

Albert Esser (1885–1972) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He earned doctorates at Heidelberg (Dr.med., ~1908–1909) and Cologne (PhD, 1926–1930), studying under Willibald Kirfel, and held posts at Heidelberg (PD 1940) and Düsseldorf (1946–1961).
